title: Decellularization and Recellularization Methodology for Human Saphenous Veins
protocol: Cut the surrounding tissue from the retrieved saphenous vein using surgical forceps and scissors.
Ligate all side branches at their ends with sutures and forceps to prevent leakage during perfusion.
Place the vein in a 50 mL tube containing 40 mL of phosphate buffer saline (PBS).
Wash the vein by changing PBS 2 - 3 times to remove excess blood.
Store the vein by freezing at -80 °C.
Connect the detergent's inlet tube to tube B using male and female Luer connectors.
Follow by connecting tube F, then tube C to the vein inlet.
Place tube F into the cassette of peristaltic pump I.
Connect one end of another tube C to the vein's outlet.
Place the other end of this tube into a glass jar with the bottom hose outlet at 45 cm above the chamber.
Securely tape both ends of the detergent inlet and outlet tubes.
Take tube G and push one end onto the hose outlet of the glass jar.
Insert the other end of tube G into the vein chamber.
Place a 1 L glass jar on a magnetic stirrer with a magnet inside the bottle.
Connect one end of tube C (detergent inlet) to the jar until it touches the bottom.
Connect the other end of this tube to tube F followed by another tube C.
Place the second tube C into the jar until it reaches half depth for the vein's inlet.
Insert tube F into the cassette of peristaltic pump I.
Attach one end of tube D to the jar at half depth for the vein’s outlet.
Connect the other end of this tube to a glass jar with the bottom hose at 45 cm height from the chamber (detergent outlet).
Secure both ends of the detergent inlet and outlet tubes.
Take a 250 mL glass bottle and place both ends of tube C into it.
Place the middle area of the tube into the cassette of peristaltic pump II.
Insert one end of the tube as the solution inlet, connect the other end to the vein's inlet.
Leave the vein's outlet free in the solution.
Place the entire setup including pump at 37 °C.
Sterilize the bioreactor by autoclaving.
To 1 L of ultrapure water, add 2 g of sodium azide and 18.6 g of ethylenediaminetetraacetic acid (EDTA). Stir until salts are dissolved.
Take 100 mL of solution 1 and add 900 mL of ultrapure water to prepare Solution 2.
To 950 mL of ultrapure water, add 50 mL of Triton X-100, 1 g of sodium azide, and 9.3 g of EDTA. Stir until dissolved for Solution 3.
Take 200 mL of solution 3 and add 800 mL of ultrapure water to prepare Solution 4.
Add 10 mL of TnBP with a 10 mL pipette to 990 mL of solution 2 to prepare Solution 5.
Add 2,000 Kunitz units of DNaseI in 50 mL of Dulbecco's Phosphate Buffer Saline containing CaCl2 and MgCl2 to prepare fresh Solution 6 for immediate use.
Add 24 g of sodium chloride, 0.6 g of potassium chloride, 4.32 g of sodium phosphate, and 0.72 g of potassium phosphate to 3 L of ultrapure water. Stir until dissolved.
Adjust the pH to 7.4 for PBS.
Sterilize 1 L of PBS in the autoclave and store separately.
To 50 mL of sterile solution 7, add 50 µL of peracetic acid to prepare fresh Solution 8 for immediate use.
Thaw human saphenous vein from -80°C at room temperature.
Freeze the vein again at -80°C and thaw at room temperature.
Cut a biopsy of 2 mm length using scissors.
Fix the biopsy in formaldehyde for 24 - 48 h at room temperature.
Tie each end of the vein to the barbs of a male and female Luer connector with a suture.
Connect the vein to decellularization setup 1 and fill with 1 L of solution 2.
Perfuse for 15 min at 35 mL/min.
Empty the contents of the setup.
Add 1 L of solution 4 and perfuse for 4 h at 35 mL/min.
Empty the contents of the setup.
Add 500 mL of solution 2 and perfuse for 5 min.
Repeat this step.
Disconnect the vein from perfusion setup 1 and connect to perfusion setup 2.
Add 1 L of solution 5, turn on the stirrer and perfuse for 4 h at 35 mL/min.
Disconnect the vein from perfusion setup 2.
Wash the outside and inside of the vein with syringe or a 10 mL pipette in 4 changes of ultrapure water for 5 - 10 min.
Connect the vein to perfusion setup 3, add 50 mL of solution 6 and perfuse at 10 mL/min in a 37 °C chamber for 4 h.
Empty the contents of the setup.
Disconnect the vein from the setup.
Connect the vein to perfusion setup 1.
Fill 1 L of solution 2 and perfuse overnight at 35 mL/min.
Repeat steps from 5.4 to 5.9 four times (for a total of five cycles).
Take a biopsy as stated in step 5.2.
Empty the contents of the setup.
Fill 1 L of solution 2 and perfuse for 24 h at 35 mL/min.
Change solution 2 after 12 h.
Empty the contents of the setup.
Fill 1 L of ultrapure water and perfuse for 24 h at 35 mL/min.
Change ultrapure water after 12 h.
Empty the contents of the setup.
Fill 1 L of solution 7 and perfuse for 24 h at 35 mL/min.
Change solution 7 after 12 h.
Wash formalin-fixed biopsies in ultrapure water for 15 min.
Process biopsies in a tissue processor following standard protocols.
Embed biopsies in paraffin.
Cut 5 µm sections using a microtome.
Stain sections with Meyer's hematoxylin and 0.2% alcoholic eosin (H&E) following standard protocols.
View under a microscope to check for loss of nuclei in decellularized tissue compared to normal tissue.
Sterilize the vein by placing it in a 50 mL tube containing 50 mL of solution 8.
Agitate at 80 rpm in the shaker for 1 h at 37 °C.
Handle the vein under the laminar flow cabinet to maintain sterility.
Transfer the vein using sterile forceps to a new 50 mL tube containing 50 mL of sterile solution 7 and 500 μL of anti-anti.
Agitate as above for 12 h.
Change Solution 7 at least twice during agitation.
Transfer the vein to a new 50 mL tube using sterile forceps after changing solutions.
Add 50 mL of endothelial media to the tube containing the vein.
Agitate as above for 11 h.
Assemble the bioreactor using sterile gloves under the laminar flow cabinet.
Tie the vein to the bioreactor's vein inlet and outlet with sterile suture and forceps.
Connect the vein to the bioreactor and fill it with endothelial media.
Add heparin at 50 IU/mL to the medium in the bioreactor.
Perfuse for 1 h at 2 mL/min at 37 °C.
Collect 15 - 25 mL of fresh blood from the donor in heparin-coated vacutainer tubes.
Dilute collected blood 1:1 with Steen solution.
Add endocrine gland-derived vascular endothelial growth factor (EG-VEGF) at 80 ng/mL to the medium.
Add basic fibroblast growth factor (b-FGF) at 4 μL/mL to the medium.
Add acetyl salicylic acid at 5 μg/mL to the medium.
Move the bioreactor to a 37 °C incubator with 5% CO2 and perfuse for 48 h at 2 mL/min.
Take a drop of blood from the bioreactor after approximately 12 h using a laminar flow cabinet.
Measure glucose levels using a blood glucose monitoring device.
If glucose level is less than 3 mmol/L, add glucose to bring it within the range of 7 - 9 mmol/L.
Repeat glucose measurement and adjustment every 8 - 12 h.
Move the bioreactor into the LAF cabinet.
Drain the blood from the bioreactor.
Add 30 mL of sterile solution 7 and perfuse for 5 min.
Drain the solution.
Repeat steps adding 30 mL of sterile solution 7, perfusing for 5 min, until the blood red color is lost.
Disconnect the vein.
Cut 5 mm edges of the vein with scissors and discard them.
Take a biopsy as stated in step 5.2 (optional).
Connect the vein again to the bioreactor (optional).
Add 30-45 mL of endothelial medium and perfuse for 96 h in the incubator at 2 mL/min.
Follow instructions in section 6 and perform H&E staining.
Examine the slides under a microscope for the presence of cells.
